description: ROC operators watch BAS and access control alarms for the 46 state, county, and city sites and dispatch technicians or alert customer security staff
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Freeze, flood, server-room temperature, and door-forced alarms need action within minutes to hours; after about 4 hours unseen alarms become damage or security exposure; alarm history newer than 1 hour is needed to dispatch correctly
manual_workaround: Fail over to the backup ROC (2 hours); until then site managers and on-call technicians walk critical sites on a schedule and customers' security staff watch door alarms locally
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-02; SYS-03; SYS-06; SYS-14; SYS-09
dependent_third_parties: Access control SaaS vendor; cloud provider; ISPs; MSSP
dependent_people_or_facilities: 23 ROC operators; on-call technicians; primary ROC; backup ROC
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,900 alarms a day across 46 sites; each hour without the ROC needs about 12 extra technician site visits
quantified_regulatory_impact: CT-S exhibit: critical alarms acknowledged within 15 minutes (performance deduction per miss); county and city addenda require 24x7 monitoring
safety_and_security_impact: Severe: freeze or flood damage, server-room overheating, or a forced door left unanswered

description: Issue and revoke badges, change door schedules, and grant event access for about 41,000 cardholders in the 4 customer tenants
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: A terminated government employee's badge must be revoked the same day; controllers cache credentials for 72 hours so doors keep working but changes stop; a lost revocation is a security gap, so the RPO is 15 minutes
manual_workaround: Customer security staff hold printed emergency revoke lists and can lock doors locally at the controller; revocations queued on paper and entered on recovery
dependent_people_or_facilities: Security Systems Manager; 21 security systems technicians
quantified_operational_impact: About 180 badge changes and 25 revocations a day across 4 tenants
quantified_regulatory_impact: Contract terms require revocation the same business day; Supervisor of Elections annex requires cage access log exports after each election
safety_and_security_impact: Severe: a terminated employee or contractor keeps access to a government building

business_process: Critical environment support (County A EOC and the state data center building)
description: Keep cooling, power monitoring, and life-safety-related building functions running at the two critical facilities, around the clock during EOC activations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The data center building overheats within hours if chilled water control fails; the EOC must stay habitable during hurricane activations; trend data older than a day has low recovery value
manual_workaround: Local operator workstations at both buildings; on-site engineer runs equipment in hand mode; portable cooling under the CT-S emergency purchase order
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; ISPs; BAS software vendor; chiller service subcontractor
dependent_people_or_facilities: On-site engineers; County A emergency management director; state data center facility lead
quantified_operational_impact: 2 buildings; during an EOC activation about 300 county and partner staff work in the EOC
quantified_regulatory_impact: County A addendum and CT-S exhibit: critical facility outages reported to the customer immediately; County A EOC is part of the county emergency plan
safety_and_security_impact: Severe: loss of the county's emergency coordination center or the state data center during an emergency

business_process: Federal building operations and maintenance (5 GSA buildings)
description: O&M of the 5 GSA buildings, including BAS operation on GSA systems through the GSA virtual desktop with PIV cards
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: GSA contract performance standards; building recovery procedures (exercised March 2026) keep the BAS running locally; loss of PIV-credentialed staff or GSA access stops remote BAS work
manual_workaround: BTTRG building recovery procedures: local operation at controllers; paper work orders
dependent_third_parties: GSA IT; GSA Public Buildings Service
quantified_operational_impact: 5 buildings, about 1.9 million sq ft; about 140 work orders a day
quantified_regulatory_impact: Performance deductions under the GSA contract quality assurance plan; FAR 52.204-21 safeguarding continues during outages
safety_and_security_impact: Moderate: building comfort and equipment protection; GSA keeps its own security systems

description: Scheduling, setpoints, trends, and alarm routing for about 9,800 BACnet controllers at 46 sites
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Controllers keep their last programs and schedules, so buildings stay usable for about a day; summer heat and event schedule changes make longer outages visible; trend data older than a day has low value
manual_workaround: Technicians change schedules at controllers or engineering workstations on site; manual-mode procedures exist only for the state sites (gap 6)
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider; ISPs; BAS software vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: 36 BAS controls technicians and engineers; building engineers
quantified_operational_impact: 46 sites; about 60 schedule changes a day; each site needs about 2 technician hours a day to run manually
quantified_regulatory_impact: SLA credits under the county and city addenda for comfort complaints not closed within 4 hours
safety_and_security_impact: Moderate: heat stress in occupied buildings in summer; equipment damage

description: Storm preparation, generator testing and runs, emergency dispatch, and post-storm building recovery for all contracts
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: During a declared emergency customers expect crews within hours; dispatch depends on contact lists, the CMMS, and mobile communications; the season runs June to November
manual_workaround: Printed storm binders with contact lists and site checklists at each regional office; satellite phones at the ROCs; radio dispatch
dependent_third_parties: Mobile carrier; CMMS vendor; generator and fuel subcontractors
dependent_people_or_facilities: Regional offices; program managers; 408 building engineers and trades
quantified_operational_impact: Up to 60 sites need pre-storm checks within 48 hours of a hurricane watch
quantified_regulatory_impact: County A and CT-S emergency response terms; County A EOC support commitments
safety_and_security_impact: Severe: life-safety systems or generators not ready when an emergency hits

business_process: Work order and preventive maintenance management
description: Create, dispatch, and close work orders and preventive maintenance for all six contracts
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Work continues from printed schedules for a few days; contract reports need complete work order history; 4-hour RPO keeps same-day dispatches
manual_workaround: Paper work orders and a shared spreadsheet; entered later
quantified_operational_impact: About 1,100 work orders a day across all contracts
quantified_regulatory_impact: Monthly performance reports to every customer depend on the work order history; missed preventive maintenance windows trigger SLA credits

business_process: Video surveillance support and evidence exports
description: Keep cameras and NVRs running; export video for customer and law enforcement investigations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: NVRs record locally, so recording continues; exports can wait a few days unless law enforcement requests them
manual_workaround: Export directly at the NVR on site
quantified_regulatory_impact: Customer contracts require exports within 2 business days of a request

business_process: Controller program engineering, backup, and restore
description: Program, back up, and restore BAS controller logic and graphics
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Needed to recover a failed or tampered controller; the repository holds current backups for only about 55% of controllers, so the real RPO for the rest is unknown (gap 6)
manual_workaround: Vendor commissioning files; reprogram from drawings (slow)
quantified_regulatory_impact: None directly; slow recovery affects BP-05 SLAs
safety_and_security_impact: Moderate: equipment run in unsafe sequences after a bad program load

business_process: School district energy management and fault analytics
description: Remote energy optimization and fault detection analytics for 62 schools on the district's BAS
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The district runs its own BAS server; the company's role is optimization and analytics, which can pause for a week
manual_workaround: District staff run schedules on their own server; analytics resume later
dependent_people_or_facilities: City and Schools Program Manager; 4 controls engineers
quantified_regulatory_impact: Monthly energy report to the district

description: Monthly deliverables, performance reports, and invoices to six customers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Monthly cycle; about $8.3 million invoiced per month; late invoices delay cash but are not lost
manual_workaround: Invoice from accounting extracts; send reports late with notice to contracting officers
quantified_operational_impact: 6 customers; about 40 invoices and 20 performance reports a month
quantified_regulatory_impact: Late reports are contract deliverable failures; interest on the credit line

description: Time capture from field tablets, biweekly payroll for 600 employees
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Biweekly payroll of about $1.5 million; wage and hour duties; field staff morale
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll with adjustments; paper timesheets
quantified_regulatory_impact: Wage payment timing duties under federal and state law

business_process: Onboarding, background checks, PIV sponsorship, and terminations
description: Hire and badge staff, coordinate PIV cards with GSA, and remove access on departure
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Terminations must still remove access the same day, across company systems and 4 customer tenants; PIV return is a FAR 52.204-9(b) duty
manual_workaround: Paper termination checklist; phone calls to customer security offices and the GSA sponsor
dependent_third_parties: HR and payroll vendor; background screening vendor; GSA PIV office
quantified_operational_impact: About 8 terminations and 10 new hires a month
quantified_regulatory_impact: FAR 52.204-9(b) PIV return; contract background check terms
safety_and_security_impact: Moderate: a departed worker keeps building access

description: Purchase equipment and services; screen against FAR 52.204-25 and 52.204-23 and FASCSA orders
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Purchases can wait a few days; screening must happen before any covered item is bought or used
manual_workaround: Hold purchases of telecommunications, video, and network equipment; emergency purchases screened manually by the Contracts Director
quantified_regulatory_impact: FAR 52.204-25(d) and 52.204-30(c) reporting if a covered item is used

description: Notify customers, contracting officers, and authorities within contract and legal deadlines; keep the notice log
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: County A requires notice within 6 hours of suspected ransomware and other contracts within 24 hours; the communication path must work even if company email is down
manual_workaround: Printed contact lists in the incident binder; out-of-band messaging group on personal phones
quantified_operational_impact: 5 customers with separate notice clocks; 1 federal contracting officer
quantified_regulatory_impact: A missed notice breaches the contract and can make the customer miss its own 12-hour or 48-hour report (Fla. Stat. 282.3185(5); 282.318(3)(c)9.c.)

description: Email, files, chat, and voice for all staff
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Most coordination runs on email and chat; ROC voice lines are separate
manual_workaround: Mobile phones and text messaging; printed contact lists
